absent.note: Murata's specification tabulates no DC-bias capacitance change; its Rating cautions only warn that a class-II capacitor's capacitance falls with applied DC voltage. Murata's product data for this part offers no characteristic graphs at all.

Murata's specification has no absolute-maximum table. Its Rating cautions bound the voltage between the terminations, surges and pulses included, by the rated voltage, which the record carries as ratings.recommended.voltage_rating; the voltage-proof test level is a production test, not a rating, and the storage conditions are for unmounted parts' solderability, not a storage-temperature limit.

/ratings/recommended/ambient_temperature.locator: page 1, section 4 Rated value, Operating Temp. Range column; page 13, Caution section 4 (Type of Applied Voltage and Self-heating Temperature)
/ratings/recommended/ambient_temperature.note: Murata's operating temperature range. Its Rating cautions hold the capacitor's own surface temperature, self-heating included, inside this range, so as a bound on ambient it is optimistic by whatever self-heating the circuit causes.

/ratings/recommended/voltage_rating.locator: page 1, section 4 Rated value, Rated Voltage column; page 2, Specifications and Test Methods item 1 (Rated Voltage); page 4, Recommended derating conditions on voltage and temperature; page 13, Caution section 3 (Applied Voltage)
/ratings/recommended/voltage_rating.note: DC 16 V. Murata defines the rated voltage as the most that may be applied continuously; with AC superimposed the larger of the peak-to-peak and zero-to-peak voltages must stay within it, and the cautions extend the bound to surges, static and pulses. Recorded as max: it is the vendor's limit for the design. This part number is one Murata designs for derated use: page 4 recommends a voltage-versus-temperature derating, published only as a graph of operating-to-rated voltage ratio against product temperature (curves for 85, 105 and 125 degC products), and its durability test runs at 100 % of rated voltage. The graph is not transcribed: reading breakpoints off it would be an estimate. The restriction is carried in the data as a string derating condition on this rating, naming the curve for 85 degC products because this part's operating range ends at 85 degC.

conditions.derating: Murata designs this part number for continuous voltage derated below the rated voltage and recommends the page 4 voltage-versus-temperature derating (curve for 85 degC products); that derating is published only as a graph and is not transcribed, so the rated voltage alone is not Murata's recommended operating voltage at every temperature.
